instrument: Safety Case Templates for Autonomous Systems (Adelard, for Dstl)
requirement_paraphrase: Argument templates for ML-enabled autonomy: requirements, hazard analysis (ODD structures scenarios), safety monitor architecture, ML-based sensor, adaptation over time, plus defeaters and evidence confidence.

instrument: Toward an Agricultural Operational Design Domain: A Framework (arXiv 2511.02937)
clause_or_section_seen: Sections 4.2 and Tables 1-2 (as described by fetch)
requirement_paraphrase: Says existing ODD concepts do not comprehensively fit agricultural/off-road machinery; proposes ODD attributes including dust (e.g. a no-dust visibility condition) and lists GNSS in a digital-information layer.

clause_or_section_seen: Sec 4-5, 5.8; Appendix B Sec VII and VI.13
requirement_paraphrase: Sets reporting categories and times (ROSI within 72 h for Cat 1; 15 calendar days for Cat 2; immediate notice for accidents/serious incidents); Appendix B lists unlawful interference with GNSS and navigation errors as reportable examples.
applies_to: UAE air operators, A6-registered aircraft, certified organisations

instrument: UAE GCAA CAR-OCR Occurrence Reporting and Aircraft Accident & Incident Investigation Regulation
edition_or_version: CAR-OCR Issue 01, Jan 2025 (as cited on GCAA page)
status_note: Cited on GCAA reporting page; text not retrieved
requirement_paraphrase: GCAA reporting page says accidents and serious incidents should be reported immediately to the Duty Investigator, and lists 'Drones or unlawful interference affecting aircraft safety' among other safety-critical events. It gives separate Safety and Security (AVSEC) duty-investigator contacts without stating which events go where, and cites AAIR and CAR-OCR (Issue 01, Jan 2025) as the legal framework, aligned with ICAO Annex 13.
applies_to: UAE civil aviation incl. drone-related events

instrument: UAE information paper to MIDANPIRG/20 & RASG-MID/10 (ICAO site)
status_note: Add: GCAA site now also lists CAR-UA-ATO Issue 01 and CAR-UAM Issue 1 (titles seen); planned CAR-Airspace Part U-space reported adopted in Mar 2025 (see C60)
requirement_paraphrase: States current UAE rules generally limit unmanned aircraft to daylight, VLOS and below 400 ft AGL, with other operations (night, BVLOS, above 400 ft, multiple UA) needing special approvals; hobbyist flights were largely kept out of controlled airspace while commercial operations have since been allowed to expand into it under approval; lists CAR-UAC, UAD, UAEV, UAX (experimental) and UAR under Federal Decree-Law 26/2022, and planned CAR-Airspace, CAR-UTMSP, CAR-UTM and CAR-USP/ASP. GNSS and remote ID not discussed.

instrument: UK CAA Regulatory Library - OSO 24 (AMC to Reg (EU) 2019/947 Art 11, Annex E)
edition_or_version: Not stated; CAA ORS9 Decision No. 46
requirement_paraphrase: Medium: design UAS to perform in environmental conditions in the flight manual, with evidence; if simulation is used, justify the target environment. High: develop to a standard acceptable to the CAA, evidence assessed by CAA.

instrument: UK CAA guidance on GNSS jamming (via SUAS News report)
status_note: Secondary press report of CAA guidance
requirement_paraphrase: Reports that CAA advises operators not to rely solely on satellite navigation during known jamming trials (be ready for alternatives such as dead reckoning), notes jamming can disable drone return-to-home and digital geofencing, and urges pilots to report jamming not announced in advance.

instrument: UK MoD Def Stan 00-056 via MOD ASEMS guidance SMP12
requirement_paraphrase: Safety case is a structured argument supported by evidence; minimum contents include requirements met, validity of requirements, SMS implemented as defined, competent key staff, and legal/standards compliance. Argument should be single and coherent.
applies_to: UK MOD acquisition programmes (binding force arises through MOD contracts, not verified here)

instrument: UK MoD JSP 936 Part 1 Dependable AI in Defence (directive)
status_note: Described as the principal MOD policy framework for AI
requirement_paraphrase: Directive covers governance, development and assurance (including safety and security) across the AI lifecycle for MOD teams.

edition_or_version: UL 3115 OOI published 31 Oct (year not on page; release dated Nov 2025); edition not stated
status_note: Outline of Investigation, not a full UL Standard; paired with UL 3300 for robots in UL certification service
requirement_paraphrase: UL says UL 3115 assesses AI-based products on robustness, reliability, transparency, accountability, privacy, fairness, safety, security and freedom from bias; UL service page says it is meant to be used with a product standard such as UL 3300 for SCIEE robots.
applies_to: AI-based products; consumer and commercial robots in homes and public spaces

status_note: Superseded by standard per other row; status of OOI not checked
requirement_paraphrase: 2020 article says UL 3300 evaluation covers multidirectional mobility, fire and shock hazards, external manipulation, user classes and use surroundings, in settings with people present.

status_note: Listed as Active (GlobalSpec); earlier 2020 Outline of Investigation
requirement_paraphrase: Covers robotic-function safety of service, communication, information, education and entertainment robots, indoor and outdoor, supplementing safety of the non-robotic function; excludes medical/care, industrial-only, people-transport, most food service, toys, hazardous-location robots.

Blog lists topics the standard covers: dependability, V&V, tool qualification, COTS and legacy components, lifecycle, maintenance, metrics/SPIs, conformance and independent assessment; three-step claim/argument/evidence structure.

status_note: ANSI webstore lists it as most recent; no amendments listed
requirement_paraphrase: Scope summary: safety principles, risk mitigation, tools, techniques and lifecycle processes for building and evaluating a safety argument for vehicles that can operate autonomously, assuming no human supervision.
applies_to: Autonomous vehicles and other autonomous products operating without human supervision (UL text names vehicles; other products per UL news page)

edition_or_version: As discussed in Koopman and Widen (arXiv 2404.16768)
requirement_paraphrase: Per the authors: UL 4600 defines safe as acceptable post-mitigation item-level risk as defined by the safety case; they cite summing total item risk (prompt element 6.1.1.3.a) as a recommended approach; UL 4600 uses SPIs and field engineering feedback for continuous improvement.
